title: parseDiff treats an added content line beginning with '++ ' as a new file header
property: an added line inside a hunk never changes the current file; changed ranges stay attributed to the right file
actual: '+++ x' (an added line with content '++ x') is parsed as a file header: file becomes 'x', a bogus entry 'x' is created and the later hunk is attributed to it, so a.txt loses range [11,11]
evidence: parseDiff is documented to parse git diff --unified=0 into file -> new-side ranges; with unified=0 added lines are printed as '+' + content, so content '++ x' yields '+++ x' inside a hunk. The parser does not track hunk line counts, so it cannot tell it from a header. Changed functions in the real file can be missed in diff mode.
